result.summary: I asked Keystone Compliance to confirm the visit date and put the ticket on hold. The tenant called to say she arranged the oven repair for 8 September 2025, but our system recorded the visit as "Monday 30/08/2025" — and 30/08/2025 was a Saturday. The contractor booked the visit, so they can settle the date. I told the tenant we are checking and that we will update her by 1 September. No escalation is needed.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord's 'Yes go ahead' (event 9) approved sending the contractor, and Keystone Compliance was assigned (events 12–14). The only open question is the visit date. Events 16–20 say 'Monday 10–12', tentative and waiting on the tenant's text, and record it as 30/08/2025, which was a Saturday. The tenant's call (event 21) says the visit was arranged for 8 Sept 2025. The contractor booked it, so they can answer. Under the 'ask before escalating' rule, I messaged the contractor and placed a hold. The tenant asked for confirmation, so she needed a reply; she got an acknowledgement with a check-back date.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The records do not confirm that date, and the guard would reject an unconfirmed date.
The contractor can settle the date; there is no cost, safety or legal issue.
The tenant asked a direct question and the records give two different dates.
